thread:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Post-incident follow-up thread for yesterday’s guardrails gating timeouts (staging + 2 pilot tenants). Please add findings + corrective actions here. Root cause doc: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PLAT/INC-2179

Sean Gallagher: Kicking off coordination. TL;DR: eval runner backlog built up, gating jobs exceeded timeout window, Optimize apply saw "timeout" state and blocked/soft-blocked depending on tier. Not customer-prod wide, but impacted pilot flow + made staging noisy.

Rafael Mendes: Adding timeline summary from notes (all times PT):
- 10:12am: first spikes in `guardrails.eval_job_queue_depth` in staging.
- 10:20am: p95 `guardrails.eval_job_latency` > 8m (SLO is 2m for pilot) -> timeouts.
- 10:28am: deploy 2025.01.03.3 included new suite selector defaults (more suites per apply) + higher min sample sizes for 2 workloads.
- 10:45am: manual scale up workers in staging from 6 -> 14, helped but queue still growing.
- 11:05am: throttled new Optimize applies in staging by toggling ff `optimize_guardrails_enforcement=observe_only`.
- 11:30am: queue drained to steady state.

Ethan Park: Control plane side: we didn’t "storm" the runner directly, but the apply endpoint now submits an eval job whenever config delta is non-empty AND cached result miss. Cache hit rate was low because prompt-set rev bumped last night (expected), but we didn’t adjust worker capacity accordingly.

Olivia Grant: +1 and suite selector change is on me. We added `tool_calling_sentinel_v2` to the default list for batching/caching changes, and also included `format_compliance` for structured output routes. That roughly doubled the prompt count for a common pilot route. I didn’t realize staging workers were sized to old suite cardinality.

Jordan Lee: From policy engine side: also worth calling out we tightened CI rule from “delta must be > threshold” to “lower bound of 90% CI must be > threshold” for 2 rubric metrics (to reduce false negatives). That increased required sample sizes for flaky graders, and job duration increased even when compute was fine.

Logan Wright: Data note: we saw the runner pulling extra artifacts to persist "gating mode" summary JSON + per-prompt traces (for pilot visibility). Artifact write time to blob store was non-trivial (~15–25s per run) and it compounded under load.

Miles Thornton: The ugly bit: our queue doesn’t have effective backpressure. Optimize apply can enqueue faster than workers can drain, and we don’t have a hard ceiling per-tenant/per-env. Once backlog hits a certain point, timeouts cascade.

Aditya Rao: From product POV: pilot customers mostly saw "Timed out" with a generic message. That’s a bad look; also we did block a couple of applies for ~40 minutes in a design partner’s sandbox. Need clearer messaging + predictable rerun behavior.

Nadia Rahman: Question: did any cost/quality metrics get polluted by partial runs? We saw some missing `eval_total_tokens` in telemetry.

Rafael Mendes: Partial runs were marked `status=timeout` but still emitted some intermediate counters. Dashboards that do naive averaging will be off. We should label incomplete runs and exclude by default.

Sean Gallagher: Agree. For corrective actions, I’m splitting into: (A) capacity/backpressure, (B) timeouts + safe-degrade, (C) observability/data hygiene, (D) release gating.

Sean Gallagher: A) Capacity/backpressure proposals:
1) Add per-env concurrency caps and per-tenant rate limits on job submission.
2) Add a "queue depth" guard that flips apply to "manual approval" (or blocks) BEFORE timeouts start.
3) Autoscale workers off queue depth + job runtime, not just CPU.

Benji Okafor: On (1), control plane can enforce a token bucket on `CreateEvalRun` by (tenant, env). We can do this in the guardrails service layer without touching Optimize. I’ll draft.

Jordan Lee: On (2), be careful: flipping enforcement modes automatically changes customer-visible behavior. But we can do a "fail closed" for pilot tiers and "manual approval" for enterprise tiers (aligns with the safe-degrade decision).

Miles Thornton: We already agreed in eng-sre thread that if runner is degraded, Dedicated enterprise can go to manual approval w/ audit, everyone else blocks. This incident shows we need the auto-detection and the playbook.

Olivia Grant: B) Timeout behavior: can we make the apply endpoint surface the eval job id and a "rerun" CTA rather than just "timeout"? Right now it looks like the platform is just broken.

Aditya Rao: +1. Also, if we have cached results for the same config delta but different prompt-set rev, we should say "needs rerun due to prompt set update" rather than generic timeout.

Logan Wright: C) Observability fixes:
- Add explicit `run_completeness` field (complete/partial/timeout) to the summary event.
- Dashboard filters default to complete only.
- Add a counter for artifact upload latency and failure rate.

Nadia Rahman: Also add a budget: artifact payload size. We saw a few 10+MB summaries when per-prompt traces got included. That’s going to hurt at scale.

Ethan Park: D) Release gating: we shipped suite selector default changes without updating staging/prod worker sizing or updating the rollout checklist. We need a step: “estimated eval workload delta” required for any change affecting suite size / sample sizes.

Connor O'Brien: From release train angle: can add a checklist item + require signoff from SRE on any PR that modifies default suites, timeouts, or min sample sizes. Even if it’s “just staging,” it becomes prod soon.

Sean Gallagher: Action items (please claim owners):
- ENG-3919: Add alerts for `eval_job_queue_depth` and `eval_job_latency` w/ paging thresholds (existing but needs tuning + staging coverage).
- NEW: Add submission rate limiting/backpressure in guardrails service (tenant/env) + 429 w/ retry-after.
- NEW: Add auto-degrade mode when backlog exceeds threshold (switch apply to block/manual approval by tier) and emit audit event.
- ENG-3914 follow-up: Worker autoscale policy based on queue depth and p95 runtime.
- ENG-3927 follow-up: Telemetry: mark incomplete runs + exclude from KPIs.
- Docs/UI: Improve timeout messaging, include job id + rerun link.

Rafael Mendes: I’ll take alerts + paging thresholds and update the rollout checklist doc. Will also add a "queue depth guard" panel to the existing dashboard (observability-pack).

Benji Okafor: I’ll take rate limiting/backpressure. Implementation idea:
- In guardrails service, before enqueue: check Redis counter for in-flight + queued per (tenant, env).
- If over limit, return `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` w/ `retry_after_seconds`.
- Add "burst" limit for staging so we don’t DOS ourselves.

Miles Thornton: I’ll take auto-degrade. We can implement a simple health gate:
- Runner health = OK if queue_depth < X AND job_latency_p95 < Y over last 5m.
- If NOT OK: apply endpoint returns deterministic “runner_degraded” outcome.
We’ll need to align with product on exact user-facing states.

Olivia Grant: I’ll take the UI/message improvements with Kenji (I’ll ping him). At minimum: show “Evaluation taking longer than expected” + “Check status” link. Ideally, async: user can navigate away and come back.

Logan Wright: I’ll take telemetry completeness + artifact latency metrics. Also propose we stop persisting per-prompt traces by default; keep behind a flag for pilot debugging.

Jordan Lee: I’ll add a note to the thresholds ADR: any change that increases min sample sizes must include runtime estimate + capacity plan, and should roll out behind `observe_only` for at least 24h.

Aditya Rao: Product will update the pilot comms: we’ll tell partners we had a staging/pilot incident, no production impact, and we’re adding backpressure + better status pages. Also will add a “rerun” button requirement to the UX spec.

Nadia Rahman: For data hygiene: I’ll update KPI definitions so “gating pass rate” excludes timeouts and partial runs, and we track timeout rate separately. Otherwise pass rate looks artificially low.

Connor O'Brien: Can we add a release guard: default suites/sample sizes changes require a feature flag + staged rollout? We shouldn’t be changing defaults “live.”

Ethan Park: +1. We have ff plumbing already (`observe_only` -> `soft_block` -> `hard_block`). We can do similar for suite selector defaults and sample sizes (pin a selector version).

Sean Gallagher: Great. Please drop PR/Linear links in-thread as they get created/updated. Also: someone update the runbook with the exact mitigation steps we used (manual scale + ff toggle) so oncall doesn’t rediscover it at 2am.

Miles Thornton: I’ll update runbook section "Runner backlog" with:
1) Check queue depth + worker saturation
2) Scale workers
3) Toggle enforcement to observe_only for staging/pilot if needed
4) Verify drain + reset
Will include commands + where in Console the flag lives.

Rafael Mendes: Adding what we should have alerted on:
- Page if staging `queue_depth > 500` for > 10m OR `job_latency_p95 > 240s` for > 10m
- Ticket if `artifact_upload_latency_p95 > 30s`
- Warn if cache hit rate < 30% after prompt-set rev bump (expected but should be visible)

Olivia Grant: One more: suite selector should output estimated prompt count and expected runtime (based on historical per-suite runtime) so we can forecast. We can build a tiny estimator using the telemetry.

Logan Wright: Yep, we already have enough data to produce `expected_runtime_seconds` by suite + model family. I can export a table for now; later we can integrate into the selector.

Sean Gallagher: Closing the loop: no further discussion needed unless new info. Next checkpoint: we review status of action items in next week’s guardrails standup.

Incident Bot: Reminder set by Sean Gallagher for 2025-01-10: “Review INC-2179 action items status in guardrails standup.” :spiral_calendar_pad:
